source.author: stat
source.text: At non et trepidis eadem sopor otia Grais suadet, et adiunctis arcet sua nubila castris noctivagi vis blanda dei: stant undique in armis foedam indignantes noctem vigilesque superbos, ecce repens superis animum lymphantibus horror Thiodamanta subit formidandoque tumultu pandere fata iubet, sive hanc Saturnia mentem, sive novum comitem bonus instigabat Apollo, prosilit in medios, visu audituque tremendus impatiensque dei, fragili quem mente receptum non capit: exundant stimuli, nudusque per ora stat furor, et trepidas incerto sanguine tendit exhauritque genas acies huc errat et illuc sertaque mixta comis sparsa cervice flagellat, sic Phryga terrificis genetrix Idaea cruentum elicit ex adytis consumptaque bracchia ferro scire vetat; quatit ille sacras in pectora pinus sanguineosque rotat crines et vulnera cursu exanimat: pavet omnis ager respersaque cultrix arbor, et attoniti currum erexere leones.
source.text_original: At non et trepidis eadem sopor otia Grais / suadet, et adiunctis arcet sua nubila castris / noctivagi vis blanda dei: stant undique in armis / foedam indignantes noctem vigilesque superbos, / ecce repens superis animum lymphantibus horror / Thiodamanta subit formidandoque tumultu / pandere fata iubet, sive hanc Saturnia mentem, / sive novum comitem bonus instigabat Apollo, / prosilit in medios, visu audituque tremendus / impatiensque dei, fragili quem mente receptum / non capit: exundant stimuli, nudusque per ora / stat furor, et trepidas incerto sanguine tendit / exhauritque genas — acies huc errat et illuc — / sertaque mixta comis sparsa cervice flagellat, / sic Phryga terrificis genetrix Idaea cruentum / elicit ex adytis consumptaque bracchia ferro / scire vetat; quatit ille sacras in pectora pinus / sanguineosque rotat crines et vulnera cursu / exanimat: pavet omnis ager respersaque cultrix / arbor, et attoniti currum erexere leones.
source.text_english: But not even the same sleep recommends rest to the anxious Greeks, and the night-roving, gentle power of the god keeps its dark clouds away from their joined camps. Guards stand everywhere in arms, grudging that foul night, and keeping proud watch. Lo, suddenly a horror comes upon Thiodamas, while his mind is bewildered by the gods, and in fearful uproar he bids them reveal the fates, whether Saturnia was driving him to this frame of mind, or good Apollo, as a new companion, was urging him on. He springs into the midst, dreadful in sight and sound, and unable to endure the god, whom a weak mind cannot contain once he has taken it in: the goads overflow, and fury stands naked through his mouth, and with uncertain blood it stretches and drains his terrified cheeks; his gaze wanders here and there, and the garlands, mixed among his hair, whip his scattered neck. So the Idaean mother draws the Phrygian, bloodied from the dread sanctuary, and forbids him, with his arms worn out by the sword, to know; he shakes the sacred pines against his breast and whirls his bloody locks, and in his rush he unnerves the wounds: all the field trembles, and the trees, sprinkled with blood, and the lions, stunned, have reared up the chariot.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Protulit ut crinem densis luctatus in extis ignis et escendit salientia viscera tauri, ecce sacer totusque dei per litora Mopsus immanis visu vittamque comamque per auras surgentem laurusque rotat.
reuse.text_original: Protulit ut crinem densis luctatus in extis / ignis et escendit salientia viscera tauri, / ecce sacer totusque dei per litora Mopsus / immanis visu vittamque comamque per auras / surgentem laurusque rotat.
reuse.text_english: As the fire, struggling amid the crowded entrails, brought forth the hair and climbed over the quivering innards of the bull, behold, the sacred Mopsus, wholly possessed by the god, terrible to see, was moving along the shore, his fillet and hair rising through the air, and he was brandishing laurel branches.
